explanations.explanation: Touch it is, friend. The people beg Jesus to touch the blind man (Mark 8:22). Not a speech, not a ceremony, just a touch. I think they knew exactly what they were asking for.

Good guess, since Jesus does teach. Mark 6:34 says He began to teach the crowd many things. But here the people beg Him to touch the man (Mark 8:22). They brought a blind man, so they came asking for a touch. Teaching is a fine thing, just not what this verse says.
Baptize is a big word, and it's not in this verse. The people beg Jesus to touch the blind man (Mark 8:22). The verse doesn't mention water at all. I'd have loved a splash, but the text says touch.

Yes, friend! Jesus takes the blind man by the hand and leads him out of the village (Mark 8:23). Think about that walk. The man can't see where he's going, and he holds on anyway. I think that's a whole lot of trust in one handhold.

The synagogue was a gathering place for worship, but this verse never goes there. Jesus leads the man by the hand out of the village (Mark 8:23). So they're walking away from the buildings, not into one. Nice try, baker.

I get the guess, but the verse doesn't say that. Jesus leads the blind man by the hand out of the village (Mark 8:23). No shoreline, no boats, just a walk out of the village. Keep the sea out of this one.

Hold on now, friend. Read the man's words again: “I can see the people, but they look like trees walking around.” (Mark 8:24) He sees something, but it isn't clear yet. So the text says he can't see everything clearly at this point. That comes next.

False is right! The man says, “I can see the people, but they look like trees walking around.” (Mark 8:24) He can see, but not clearly yet. I think that's a wild thing to say out loud, and honestly, I respect his honesty.

explanations.answer: Places His hands on his eyes again
explanations.explanation: That's it! Jesus places His hands on the man's eyes once again (Mark 8:25). The man told Jesus what he saw, and Jesus went right back to work. Nobody gets hurried out the door here. I like that a lot.

explanations.answer: Sends him to wash in a pool
explanations.explanation: John 9:7 has a man told to wash in the pool of Siloam, but that's a different story. Here, Jesus places His hands on the man's eyes again (Mark 8:25). No washing in this one. Jesus stays right there with him.

explanations.answer: Tells him to come back later
explanations.explanation: Nope, no coming back later. Jesus places His hands on the man's eyes once again (Mark 8:25). The man isn't sent away to return another day. I'd stay put, too, friend.
True! When the man opens his eyes, his sight is restored, and he can see everything clearly (Mark 8:25). From trees walking around to clear as day. Friend, that's a big change in one moment.

I see why you'd pause, since the man said the people looked like trees walking around (Mark 8:24). But the text says his sight was restored, and he could see everything clearly (Mark 8:25). So this one is true. Trees walking around are behind him now.

explanations.answer: Do not go back into the village
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker! Jesus sends him home and says, “Do not go back into the village.” (Mark 8:26) The text doesn't say why, so I won't guess a reason. I'll just say it's a good one to remember word for word.

explanations.answer: Go tell everyone in the village
explanations.explanation: Pretty natural idea, but it's the opposite of what Jesus says. He tells the man, “Do not go back into the village.” (Mark 8:26) The text doesn't give a reason, so I'm not going to make one up. Just remember He sends him home.

explanations.answer: Go show yourself to the priests
explanations.explanation: That line belongs to a different healing, where Jesus tells a man to show himself to the priest (Matthew 8:4). Here, He says, “Do not go back into the village.” (Mark 8:26) Same Jesus, different moment. Easy mix-up, friend.
